[Autofill] Parse mandatory re-auth status in GetUnmaskDetailsRequest

Add mandatory_reauth_status and fido_creation_options to
payments::UnmaskDetails and parse them from the GetDetailsForGetRealPan
response.

mandatory_reauth_status is the state (unknown, disabled or enabled) of
the mandatory re-auth setting that the Payments server stores for the
device. It stays unset when the response does not carry a status this
client knows, so that mandatory re-auth is only treated as
server-controlled when the server says so.

fido_creation_options is the WebAuthn creation challenge that the
server pre-fetches for a device that is expected to enroll into FIDO
authentication while unmasking a card.

Neither field is consumed yet.

Design: go/server-controlled-mandatory-reauth-chrome-dd
HLD: go/autofill-reauth-hld

[OpenScreen] Fix Cast perf test startup tracing, CrOS, and crash logs

Fix six test harness bugs uncovered while investigating
mediarouter-perf failures:

1. Pass categories via --trace-startup=<categories> with
   --trace-startup-record-mode=record-continuously. Chromium has no
   --trace-startup-categories switch, so bare --trace-startup recorded
   every default browser category (~120 MB per 45s clip).
2. Backfill typing.override and typing.TypeAliasType from
   typing_extensions in cros_setup._prepare_crossbench_imports() so
   Crossbench imports succeed under Chromium's Python 3.11 vpython
   environment.
3. Store ChromeOS sender startup traces and Chrome debug logs in
   /var/log/chrome, send SIGTERM to Chrome during teardown so the
   startup trace is flushed, and fall back to streaming over SSH when
   scp is blocked by SELinux.
4. Stop retrying SessionNotCreatedException 20 times in
   connect_to_remote_driver(), dump remote logs when
   setup_test_environment() fails before cleanup deletes them, and read
   chromedriver_*.log so verbose Chrome stderr crash logs are captured.
5. Fall back to caseNameComponents=['*fixture'] when ResultSink rejects
   multi-part case names under the "single" module scheme.
6. Drop track_event_config from the receiver Perfetto config. The
   Android 12 perfetto binary on the Chromecast rejects the field, so
   no receiver traces were recorded at all.

[Contextual Tasks] Add tab context menu unshare UI test

Adds an interactive UI test covering unsharing a tab from AI Mode
through the tab strip context menu (CommandAiModeUnshare) for signed-in
and signed-out users (skipped in Incognito, where tab sharing is
unavailable). The test protects the unshare item and its
ContextualTasksSidePanelCoordinator::UnshareTabs() dispatch against
regressions.

This tests the following CUJ:
 (1) User has an AI Mode thread that was started from Tab 0.
 (2) User shares Tab 1 with that thread from the tab context menu's
     AI Mode share submenu.
 (3) The Contextual Tasks side panel opens with Tab 1 selected, and
     Tab 1 shows the AI Mode sharing tab alert and tab underline.
 (4) User opens the tab context menu on Tab 1 and clicks the AI Mode
     unshare item.
 (5) Tab 1 is no longer selected in the side panel, and no longer shows
     the AI Mode sharing tab alert or tab underline.
 (6) The unshare item is no longer offered in Tab 1's tab context menu.

Key Implementation Details:
- User Variations: Runs in the parameterized
  ContextualTasksTabSubMenuInteractiveUiTest across kSignedIn,
  kSignedOut, and kIncognito. Incognito is skipped because
  CanShareTabContext() is false for OTR profiles.
- Menu Dispatch: Builds the real TabMenuModel for Tab 1's TabHandle and
  activates the unshare item through a delegate that forwards to
  TabStripModel::ExecuteContextMenuCommand(), as
  TabContextMenuController does.
- Side Panel Selection: Checks the side panel thread's
  ContextualTasksWebContentsUserData::GetSelectedTabs(), which feeds the
  composebox's selected tabs.
- Tab Underline: Checks the glic::TabUnderlineView on Tab 1's tab strip
  anchor view.
- Synchronization: Polls the sharing alert, side panel selection, and
  tab underline with PollingStateObservers for both the share and
  unshare transitions.

Verification:
- Local: 20/20 consecutive passes per variant via tools/autotest.py
  (SignedIn, SignedOut; Incognito skipped)
- Swarm: 10/10 shards via tools/run-swarmed.py (SignedIn 50/50,
  SignedOut 50/50, Incognito skipped; 0 flakes)

[Omnibox] Remove unused kOmniboxFuseboxAsyncInflation flag

The OmniboxFuseboxAsyncInflation feature was added to gate inflating the
Fusebox RecyclerView on a background thread, but no code ever checks it:
neither C++ nor the Java CachedFlag sFuseboxAsyncInflation has any
readers. The flag expired in M160, so remove its declaration, the Java
export, the chrome://flags entry and metadata, and the fieldtrial
testing config. This is a no-op for behavior.

openh264rs: Disable code coverage instrumentation

Rust targets, matching //third_party/rust crates.

fills byte-by-byte, causing severe slowdown and test timeouts on coverage
bots.

[Views] Clamp hosted child bubbles to their hosting root window bounds

On X11, parented TYPE_BUBBLE widgets use NativeWidgetAura hosted inside
the parent browser widget's DesktopNativeWidgetAura root window, so any
part of the bubble extending outside the browser window is clipped.

Intersect available bounds in BubbleFrameView::GetUpdatedWindowBounds
with the hosting root window's screen bounds when the bubble is hosted
inside another widget's DesktopNativeWidgetAura, and enable bounds
adjustment in BubbleDialogDelegate::GetBubbleBounds for such hosted
bubbles unless adjust_if_offscreen was explicitly disabled. Bubbles that
own their own DesktopNativeWidgetAura (Wayland, Windows) and non-desktop
Aura roots (ChromeOS) are unaffected.

[iOS] Show the non-modal sign-in promo as a banner overlay

The non-modal sign-in promo was an InfobarCoordinator banner presented
by the BVC. While it was showing, other UI, such as the bookmarks
editor, either failed to present or was presented on top of it and
dismissed along with it when it timed out.

It is now a Confirm infobar on the active tab, presented by the infobar
banner overlay like other banners. NonModalSignInPromoInfoBarDelegate
provides the banner content, NonModalSignInPromoMediator owns the promo
lifecycle, dismissal triggers, metrics and IPH bookkeeping, and
NonModalSignInPromoCoordinator keeps view-visibility gating and sign-in
presentation.

Behavior changes:
- The promo is skipped, without using an IPH impression, if the browser
  view isn't in the view hierarchy (e.g. tab grid) or a banner is
  already showing.
- It is dismissed when the active tab changes, the browser view leaves
  the view hierarchy, or another banner is added or shown.
- It times out after the default banner duration and stays until
  dismissed when VoiceOver is running.
- Banner metrics are recorded under the Confirm infobar type.

media: Fix EOS race in MediaFoundation track-switch browsertest

Playback_EncryptedCencVideoAudio_TrackSwitch uses 2.74s encrypted video
clips while MediaFoundationRenderer polls statistics every 500ms.
Waiting for two frame-count updates on track 0 and two more on track 1
consumes roughly the full clip duration, so switching back to track 0
often lands right at end-of-stream.

When OnTracksChanged overlaps EOS, PipelineController is in
SWITCHING_TRACKS and WebMediaPlayerImpl drops the OnEnded signal before
looping can seek back to zero. MediaFoundation then flushes and restarts
track 0 at the end of the timeline where no video frames remain to
decode. Rewinding to t=0 before each track switch keeps the switch in
active playback and lets us re-enable the skipped Windows GPUs.

This eliminates the 39.5s track-switch timeouts in
media_foundation_browser_tests on Windows and restores coverage across
the 4 skipped GPU models.

[CCA] Load colors.css before starting ColorChangeUpdater

setupDynamicColor() previously called ColorChangeUpdater.forDocument()
before awaiting chrome://theme/colors.css. CameraAppUI's constructor
already sets the dark mode override, and ColorChangeHandler::SetPage()
immediately triggered OnColorProviderChanged() -> refreshColorsCss(),
which removed the in-flight colors.css <link> before its load event
fired and hung camera startup before view-camera became active.

Await loadCSS() first, attach one-shot load/error listeners so failed
loads reject rather than hang, and then start ColorChangeUpdater.

[Contextual Tasks] Add Thread History overflow menu UI test

Adds an interactive UI test covering the Thread History item in the
rearchitecture side panel toolbar's overflow menu, across all user
variations (signed-in, signed-out, and incognito).

This tests the following CUJ:
 (1) User opens Lens Overlay from the 3-dot App Menu on a web page.
 (2) User types a query into the Lens Overlay Contextual Searchbox and
     presses Enter to submit.
 (3) The Contextual Tasks side panel opens on an AI Mode page.
 (4) User clicks the toolbar overflow menu button.
 (5) User clicks the Thread History item in the overflow menu.
 (6) The overflow menu closes and the browser posts an OpenThreadsView
     message to the AI Mode page in the side panel.

Key Implementation Details:
- User Variations: Parameterized via
  ContextualTasksInteractiveTestBaseT<UserVariation> across kSignedIn,
  kSignedOut, and kIncognito.
- Message Verification: Records the ClientToSearchMessages posted to
  the side panel page with SetSearchMessageDispatcherForTesting() and
  completes the search channel handshake, then polls for exactly one
  OpenThreadsView message after the click.
- Anti-Flakiness: Waits for the side panel page to load and the
  toolbar thread title to update before opening the menu, and waits
  for the menu and Thread History item to render before clicking.

Verification:
- Local: 20/20 consecutive passes per variant via tools/autotest.py
  (60/60 total)
- Swarm: 50/50 passes per variant across 10 bots via
  tools/run-swarmed.py (150/150 total, 0 flakes across 10 shards)

[UnboundedElement] Enable ChildWindowRealignedOnWidgetMove in tests

CL https://crrev.com/c/8831127 gated top-level owned Aura window move
realignment in DesktopNativeWidgetTopLevelHandler behind the
default-disabled ChildWindowRealignedOnWidgetMove feature, enabling it
only via fieldtrial_testing_config.json. In Chrome-branded builds (where
the fieldtrial testing config is not applied),
UnboundedElementBrowserTest cases that move an unbounded surface without
resizing (MoveWithoutResize, SubframeSurfaceFollowsEmbedderRelayout, and
SubframeSurfaceFollowsZoomChange) time out because the owned surface
window is not realigned on widget moves.

Move kChildWindowRealignedOnWidgetMove from ui/views/views_features to
ui/base/ui_base_features (so content/ can reference it directly) and
enable it via ScopedFeatureList::InitAndEnableFeature in
UnboundedElementBrowserTestBase on Aura platforms. Otherwise, this test
fails 100% on branded builds.

[Linux] RPM: run the daily repo/key job from a systemd timer

The RPM only installed /etc/cron.daily/@@PACKAGE but does not require a
cron implementation, and Fedora (since 36) and openSUSE no longer
install one by default. On those systems the job never runs, so the
package signing key is never imported or refreshed (the job is the only
place that happens since the import was dropped from %post) and the
repo file is never repaired.

Ship @@PACKAGE-repo.service and @@PACKAGE-repo.timer in
/usr/lib/systemd/system that run the same script daily
(Persistent=true, randomized delay). As in the Debian package, the
script now lives in @@INSTALLDIR/cron/@@PACKAGE and
/etc/cron.daily/@@PACKAGE is a symlink to it, so systems with cron keep
working (the script is idempotent, so running it from both is
harmless). %post enables the timer whenever systemctl exists and only
reloads/starts it when systemd is running, so installs in containers
and image builds keep working; %preun disables it on uninstall. Users
can opt out with "systemctl mask".

Tested in a fedora:43 container (no cron): fresh install without
systemd, upgrade from the previous layout (regular cron.daily file ->
symlink, timer enabled), reinstall, masked timer stays masked, erase
removes the units and the timers.target.wants link. Running the unit's
ExecStart imports the Google signing key and writes the repo file.

Disallow partitioned cookies on cross-origin doc prefetches

Cross-origin restricted main-frame prefetches and their recursive
preload subresources use a destination-origin IsolationInfo so
responses populate the destination's HTTP cache partition. However,
deriving a CookiePartitionKey from that IsolationInfo also scopes
cookie access to the destination's top-level cookie partition.

Add CookieSettingOverride::kForceDisablePartitionedCookies and set it
in URLLoaderFactoryParamsHelper::CreateForPrefetch(), while disabling
Device Bound Session Credentials on cross-origin and recursive
prefetches in PrefetchURLLoaderServiceContext:

- Enforce kForceDisablePartitionedCookies in CookieSettingsBase and
  network::CookieSettings so partitioned cookies are blocked even when
  unpartitioned cookies are allowed, while keeping
  URLRequest::cookie_partition_key() (including nonces) intact.
- Omit reading non-nonced partitioned cookies in URLRequestHttpJob and
  omit partition metadata in HandleClearSiteDataHeader() and DevTools
  raw request/response notifications when the override is active.

infra: Default chromium.linux ci builders to be ssd-agnostic

Two builders in chromium.linux were promoted from chromium.fyi after
https://crrev.com/c/8465642 landed (linux-webdriver-bidi-rel and
linux-arm64-rel). Because they didn't set ssd=None, they inherited the
default "ssd:0" dimension and got pinned to the last 13 HDD bots in
luci.chromium.ci (luci-chromium-ci-cronet-jammy-us-central1-b-8).

So this sets ssd=None in chromium.linux's defaults (and drops the
redundant per-builder overrides). That makes those two builders
ssd-agnostic so they can run on the main C3+SSD pool, and keeps newly
added builders here from picking up "ssd:0" by accident.

Ash: Move power button menu to a client-owned widget

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to move Ash widgets off
the deprecated NATIVE_WIDGET_OWNS_WIDGET and WIDGET_OWNS_NATIVE_WIDGET
ownership modes and onto CLIENT_OWNS_WIDGET, the mode views recommends
for all widgets. With it, the code that creates a widget owns it and
decides when it is destroyed. This removes a common source of dangling
pointers and window teardown bugs.

The power button controller already owned its menu widget. When the
controller destroys the widget, its window is now hidden at once and
destroyed a task later instead of immediately, with no visible change.

[Cast Streaming] Clamp video capture framerate to receiver constraints

OpenscreenSessionHost::SetConstraints() clamps the video sender
framerate to the receiver's capture recommendations, but leaves video
capture configured at the initial target rate. With 60 FPS capture
enabled against a receiver that caps output to 30 FPS (or omits display
constraints and defaults to 30 FPS), capture keeps delivering 60 FPS
into a 30 FPS sender, causing burst frame drops and false congestion
backoff.

Clamp MirrorSettings to the lower of the current capture rate and the
receiver's recommended maximum framerate when positive, keeping capture,
encoding, and sending aligned while ignoring omitted or non-positive
frame rates. Also fix the session host unit test harness so custom test
ANSWER messages are sent instead of ignored.

IndexedDB: fix within-transaction Blob key comparison

The LevelDB store keeps blob handles in memory during a single r/w
transaction, or indefinitely in the case of incognito. These in-memory
blobs are keyed on serialized strings, but did a byte-wise comparison
instead of the special comparator that the database uses.

cc: Let a raster target request that image precision be preserved

SoftwareImageDecodeCache and GpuImageDecodeCache are each constructed
with a fixed SkColorType in which to store decoded images.

Some clients (the ones in blink) create two caches -- one for F16 and
one for N32, and choose the caches for each image based on various
one-off questionable logic.

Other clients (tile rasterization) specify the tile format as the target
color type, and convert everything they can to that.

Prepare to get rid of the N32-and-F16 scheme. Add
TargetColorParams::preserve_image_precision as the way for an image
decoder cache client to say "don't crush this to the cache's
SkColorType".

Nothing sets the new parameter yet. A follow-up will use it to remove
the separate N32 and F16 caches in Blink.

Update the logic in both caches to respect this, and to also use the
function PaintImage::DecodeCacheColorConversionIsDestructive. The logic
in those functions is still a bit bespoke, and can be further simplified
later.

Fix Avatar feature-parity audit issue F15 (P2/R3)

When kInitialWebUI and kWebUIAvatarButton are enabled without
kWebUIToolbar (the partial-WebUI configuration), JS layout in app.ts is
disabled. The C++ WebUIToolbarWebView::ComputeLayout() logic hardcoded
the avatar button size to the base button width.

This CL fixes two bugs in partial WebUI mode:
1. Profiles where !AvatarToolbarButton::CanShowForProfile(browser_)
   (e.g., DevTools profiles) reserved an empty 34px button slot.
2. Labeled avatar chips were clipped at 34px because the C++ layout did
   not reserve their actual text width.

This implements GetAvatarControlWidth() to dynamically calculate the
rendered width based on AvatarControlState, and updates ComputeLayout()
to reserve 0 width when hidden and the actual text width when shown. It
also ensures OnPreferredSizeChanged() is triggered when the text or
visibility changes.

Remove redundant debugger-step-over.js web test

Delete the legacy web test
http/tests/devtools/sources/debugger-step/debugger-step-over.js
and its expectation file instead of migrating to inspector-protocol.

The legacy test pauses on a debugger statement inside a helper
function, invokes Debugger.stepOver twice to step over a synchronous
call f() without entering it, and verifies the call stack at each
pause before resuming. This exercises V8 stepping mechanics without
Blink-specific behavior.

Existing tests already cover every layer:
- V8: v8/test/inspector/debugger/step-over.js (with testProcedure in
  v8/test/inspector/debugger/resources/break-locations.js and
  v8/test/inspector/debugger/step-over-expected.txt) verifies
  Debugger.stepOver steps across procedure() calls without entering.
- Blink: third_party/blink/web_tests/inspector-protocol/debugger/
  step-over-caught-exception.js and stepping-with-blackboxed-ranges.js
  exercise Debugger.stepOver over Blink CDP sessions.
- DevTools: front_end/core/sdk/DebuggerModel.test.ts ("keeps the step
  context across instrumentation pauses" / "clears the step context
  when the user resumes"), front_end/models/bindings/
  SourceMapStepping.test.ts, and test/e2e/sources/
  inline-variable.test.ts / sourcemap.test.ts (STEP_OVER_BUTTON ->
  SourcesPanel.stepOver -> DebuggerModel.stepOver) cover SDK, bindings,
  and UI stepping end-to-end.

Ash: Make the screen switch check controller own its dialog widgets

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to move Ash widgets off
the deprecated NATIVE_WIDGET_OWNS_WIDGET and WIDGET_OWNS_NATIVE_WIDGET
ownership modes and onto CLIENT_OWNS_WIDGET, the mode views recommends

pointers and window teardown bugs.

as soon as it closes or its window goes away.

[X11] Resolve six X11, Ozone, and GBM TODOs

Resolve six stale or small X11 TODOs across ui/base/x,
ui/ozone/platform/x11, and ui/gfx/linux:

- Remove dead ui::IsX11WindowFullScreen(), which has no callers.
- Populate _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW data[2] with the requestor's currently
  active X11Window (queried from X11WindowManager before clearing
  ignore_keyboard_input_), as recommended by EWMH, and add a unit test
  verifying the ClientMessage payload.
- Replace the X11Window::Map() flush TODO with the verified reason:
  non-GLib builds (such as CastOS and Linux-ChromeOS) use
  X11EventWatcherFdWatch, which has no pre-poll flush hook before
  MessagePumpEpoll sleeps, leaving MapWindow buffered when going idle;
  add a unit test covering async window mapping without an explicit
  Sync().
- Document why X11SoftwareBitmapPresenter reads
  CHROMIUM_COMPOSITE_WINDOW from the X11 server across processes and
  drop the obsolete DRI3 software-compositing TODO.
- Document why kRGBA_1010102 remains disabled during GBMSupportX11
  startup format probing.

873bace9141c55c54455a845b56e8ec3f7fbe0d1 [ diff ] 
Add a use counter for media playing while skipped by content-visibility

css-contain-2 defines that a media element whose contents are skipped by
'content-visibility: hidden' has its audio output suppressed and its
events deferred (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain-2/#cv-notes item
12). Before changing that behavior in Chrome, measure how much content
it would affect.

The counter fires from the playback progress timer, so it counts pages
where a media element is actually playing inside skipped contents, in
the same document or across a frame boundary, rather than pages that
merely set the property.

IsInContentVisibilityHiddenSubtreeCrossingFrames() is the 'hidden'-only
counterpart of IsInLockedSubtreeCrossingFrames(); contents skipped by
'content-visibility: auto' are exempt per the spec, since they are
off-screen but may remain relevant to the user.

Ash: Make the Phone Hub app stream error dialog own its widget

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to move Ash widgets off
the deprecated NATIVE_WIDGET_OWNS_WIDGET and WIDGET_OWNS_NATIVE_WIDGET
ownership modes and onto CLIENT_OWNS_WIDGET, the mode views recommends
for all widgets. With it, the code that creates a widget owns it and
decides when it is destroyed. This removes a common source of dangling
pointers and window teardown bugs.

The object that anchors the Phone Hub app stream error dialog now owns
the dialog's widget instead of holding a raw pointer to it, and destroys
the widget when it closes or its parent bubble or window goes away.

[Media] Add StreamParser::HasUnparsedData for MP4 and MPEG audio

Expose a virtual HasUnparsedData() method on StreamParser so
segment-based demuxers can detect when an append ended inside an
incomplete MP4 box or MPEG audio frame/tag rather than on a clean
container boundary.

I've included the MP4 as an implementation as well, since it's so
trivially simple. MP2T is significantly more complicated and it's in a
follow up CL so it's easier to review.

[Public Transit] Add best_practices.md for authoring and review

Collect the authoring and code-review conventions for Public Transit
tests and Transit Layer code into best_practices.md:
- Transit vs. Test Layer separation, concrete return types, Element
  interactions, To()/verb/Outcome naming, and ConditionWithResult
  Elements via declareEnterConditionAsElement().
- Reusable one-shot Outcomes (reach(), after(), replacedBy(),
  returning()).
- Element scoping, RootSpec defaults, WebPageFacility/HtmlElement DOM
  checks, optional affordances, destination expectations, batching
  hygiene, custom UiThreadConditions with waitForAnd(), multi-window
  inNewTask()/reachLastStop()/rotateTo(), *Fast() helpers, ViewFinder,
  and incremental hop-on test-util conversion (hopOnAt()/hopOnTo()).

Part 2 of 4 establishing updated in-tree Public Transit documentation
and the public-transit agent skill.

[Extensions] Add chrome.sidebar.getLayout()

`chrome.sidebar` is an empty namespace. Extensions that adopt it cannot
query which side of the window the panel uses, which
`chrome.sidePanel.getLayout()` already supports.

After this change, `chrome.sidebar.getLayout()` resolves with a
`PanelLayout` whose `side` is "left" or "right", the same result as
`chrome.sidePanel.getLayout()`. The API stays behind the `ApiSidebar`
flag on the trunk channel.

Add the `Side` enum, `PanelLayout` and `getLayout()` to sidebar.webidl
and implement `SidebarGetLayoutFunction` on top of
`SidePanelService::GetSidePanelLayout()`. The `sidebar` schema defines
its own types, so the function converts the `sidePanel` side to the
`sidebar` side. Add the SIDEBAR_GETLAYOUT histogram value.

[DefaultBrowser] Watch parent UrlAssociations keys on Windows

On modern Windows 11 builds, default protocol association updates can be
written to sibling subkeys under UrlAssociations\{http,https} (such as
UserChoiceLatest) without modifying the legacy UserChoice subkey.
Watching only the child UserChoice keys misses these updates, leaves the
monitor partially or fully inactive if watched keys are absent on
startup, and fires without debouncing on rapid registry updates.

Gate watching the permanent parent UrlAssociations\{http,https} keys
behind the new DefaultBrowserMonitorUrlAssociations feature (enabled by
default as a kill switch). When enabled, DefaultBrowserMonitor re-arms
immediately on change, upgrades the watcher if any watched keys were
missing during an earlier StartMonitor call, and coalesces subtree write
bursts with a trailing-edge debounce timer (400ms default).

media/gpu: Decode AV1 spatial layers with VideoToolbox behind a flag

WebRTC AV1 streams with spatial layers (L2T2, L3T3, ...) always fall
back to software decoding: RTCVideoDecoderAdapter, AV1Decoder and the
AV1 ResolutionMonitor all refuse them. VideoToolbox can decode them,
since VideoToolboxAV1Accelerator already hands it the whole temporal
unit and VideoToolbox returns the top layer.

Add kVideoToolboxAV1SpatialLayerDecoding (Mac only, disabled by
default) and media::IsAV1SpatialLayerHWDecodingEnabled(), true on
macOS 26 or later with the feature enabled. When it is true:

 * VideoToolboxAV1Accelerator::SupportsSpatialLayers() returns true.
   The accelerator describes the format by the sequence max frame size,
   since the first frame of a temporal unit changes size whenever an
   SFU changes the forwarded layers and an av1C cannot be rebuilt from
   a delta frame. It sets serialize_decodes for sequences with spatial
   layers, detected from the sequence header or from a temporal unit
   with more than one shown frame.
 * RTCVideoDecoderAdapter (for the VideoToolbox decoder only) and
   Av1ResolutionMonitor accept AV1 spatial layers.

macOS 26 is the oldest version tested: VideoToolbox output matched
libdav1d bit-exactly on M3 Pro, M4 and M5 Pro for L1T2, L2T1, L3T1,
L2T3, L3T3, L3T3 simulcast, L3T3_KEY and mid-stream layer drops (see
the bug). As a viewer of four 1080p L3T2 presenters in a 300-person
call, renderer plus GPU process CPU went from about 220% (dav1d) to
about 87% (VideoToolbox).

Streams whose sequence header declares too low a level for their top
layer still fail libgav1's level check and fall back to software
decoding, as non-SVC streams do today.

Bug: 573939397
Test: blink_platform_unittests
      --gtest_filter=RTCVideoDecoderAdapterTest.*:*ResolutionMonitor*
Test: Manual WebRTC loopback with --enable-features=
      VideoToolboxAV1SpatialLayerDecoding. L2T2 640x480 and L3T2
      1280x720 decode on VideoToolbox (powerEfficientDecoder=true),
      including the top layers being dropped and restored mid-stream.
      Without the feature the same streams fall back to dav1d.

[gpu] Track link generation for program info updates

Previously, asynchronous program reflection updates returned from the
passthrough command decoder identified the target program only by its
client ID. When a program was relinked while a parallel shader
completion query was still pending, the late reflection data from the
earlier link could populate the newly recreated client cache entry and
cause uniform queries to allocate undersized stack buffers.

Track a per-program link count across the client cache, return data wire
format, and passthrough service queries so stale program info updates
are ignored. Synchronous cache fills re-check the program after the
unlocked IPC, since another context in the share group may relink or
delete it in the meantime. Blink also cleans up superseded completion
queries.

Optimize and modernize BluetoothUUID

Accept std::string_view in the BluetoothUUID string constructor to avoid
unnecessary string allocations.

In addition, this change:
- Avoids redundant storage for 128-bit UUIDs by having value() return
  canonical_value_ directly for 128-bit formats.
- Implements explicit move constructors and assignment operators that
  reset the moved-from instance to an invalid state.
- Modernizes string formatting with absl::StrFormat and base::StrCat.
- Optimizes Windows GUID conversion and constructor logic.
- Passes BluetoothUUID by const reference in operator<<.

[ContextualTasks] Match Lens focus color to AIM

Because `lens_button.html` runs inside a component extension whose CSP
only allows chrome://resources/*, it cannot load
chrome://theme/colors.css and leaves
`--color-searchbox-results-icon-focused-outline` unset. Its fallback
values (#0b57d0 in light mode and #a8c7fa in dark mode) differ from the
#336ef3 focus ring used by sibling AI Mode input plate buttons in both
color schemes.

Update the `#lensButton` focus outline fallback to #336ef3 in both light
and dark modes so keyboard focus on the Lens button matches adjacent AI
Mode buttons, while keeping Highlight under forced-colors mode.

Move more notifications to WebLocalFrameMetricsObserver

Move DidLoadResourceFromMemoryCache, OnMainFrameRectangleChanged,
OnMainFrameViewportRectangleChanged, and OnMainFrameAdRectangleChanged
notifications directly to WebLocalFrameMetricsObserver.

This simplifies the plumbing by bypassing WebLocalFrameClient,
RenderFrame, and RenderFrameObserver, and removes the corresponding
deprecated methods and callbacks from content/ and blink client
interfaces. Tracking and deduplication of main frame and viewport
rectangles are now handled directly in WebLocalFrameImpl.

[iOS] Defer Picture-in-Picture start until transitions finish

Default browser promos dismiss their sheet on BrowserViewController and
synchronously request Picture-in-Picture instructions. Because the promo
dismissal animation is still in progress on the base view controller,
UIKit drops the Picture-in-Picture modal presentation and neither
Picture-in-Picture nor iOS Settings opens.

Wait for active transitions on baseViewController via
ExecuteWhenTransitionsComplete() before starting
PictureInPictureCoordinator, and guard against cancelled or superseded

[search] Stop tab search panel from recoloring system bars

SearchUiCoordinator set the status and navigation bar colors of its
hosting activity whenever it applied its color scheme. That is correct
for SearchActivity, but the tab search panel embeds the coordinator in
the tabbed activity, so opening the panel recolored the tabbed window's
bars and never restored them.

Move the system bar coloring back into SearchActivity, where it lived
before the search box UI was split out into SearchUiCoordinator, and
stop passing the tabbed activity's EdgeToEdgeSystemBarColorHelper to
TabSearchOverlayCoordinator.

Move Windows/x86/SwiftShader tests to GCE

Moves the test coverage for suites on the Chromium/Dawn Windows x86
testers that use SwiftShader to run on the newly set up software
renderer testers. This should be a functional no-op in terms of test
behavior, but deduplicates some test coverage and frees up a bit of
real hardware capacity.

The following suites are moved:

* telemetry_gpu_unittests
* webgpu_swiftshader_blink_web_tests
* webgpu_swiftshader_blink_web_tests_with_backend_validation
* webgpu_swiftshader_web_platform_cts_tests
* webgpu_swiftshader_web_platform_cts_with_validation_tests

This also moves the tests to run using WARP instead of SwiftShader
since SwiftShader is on its way out and the Dawn team agreed to
prioritize testing WARP.

TranslatorImpl::Translate previously passed the address of its const
input reference as user_data to TranslateCallback, mutating the caller's

instead so the input string stays untouched, and allow a null buffer
pointer when buffer_size is zero.

[glic] Gate GlicFeature::kDynamicChromeTools to non-Android platforms

GlicWebClientHandler::CreateAiOverlayTools is only implemented on
non-Android platforms (#if !BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)), whereas
GeminiGlicProviderSpec::SupportsFeature previously returned
base::FeatureList::IsEnabled(kGlicDynamicChromeTools) unconditionally
across all platforms.

Gate GlicFeature::kDynamicChromeTools behind #if !BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)
so Android does not advertise HostCapability::kChromeTools before
Android Glic tool execution is implemented.

[GEiC] Don't switch provider if the Settings restart is cancelled

The Settings buttons that switch between Gemini and Gemini Enterprise
saved the new provider before restarting Chrome. If an Incognito window
was open, the restart confirmation dialog appeared, and cancelling it
still left the new provider to take effect at the next restart.

The switch is now saved only once the restart is confirmed. To support
this, RelaunchMixinLit.performRestart() takes an optional callback that
runs right before the restart. <relaunch-confirmation-dialog> now just
closes when confirmed, and the mixin's close handler runs the callback
and restarts if wasConfirmed(). Other Settings pages behave as before.

Known limitation: if a page's "Leave site?" prompt cancels the restart
after it's confirmed, the switch still takes effect at the next restart,
as it already did without the dialog.

[webapps] Defer shortcut DialogAction metric when app type is unknown

When the Universal Install bottom sheet appears after its 3.5-second
timeout while the native installability check is still running, mAppType
remains null. Tapping "Create shortcut" in that window previously
unboxed null in the mAppType == AppType.SHORTCUT comparison in
onAddShortcutClicked() (where assumeNonNull(mAppType) only suppressed
NullAway at compile time) and threw a NullPointerException.

Remove assumeNonNull(mAppType), extract recordAddShortcut(@AppType int
appType), and only invoke it immediately when mAppType is non-null;
otherwise defer recording CREATE_SHORTCUT or CREATE_SHORTCUT_TO_APP in
WebApk.UniversalInstall.DialogAction until onAppDataFetched() completes,
matching the existing catch-up pattern used for DialogShownForAppType.

infra: Reduce blink_wpt_tests shards from 7 to 3 on Win and Mac

Win10 Tests x64 and mac26-arm64-rel-tests (plus win-rel and mac-rel)
currently split blink_wpt_tests across 7 shards even though each shard
runs only ~46s of tests on Mac and ~141s on Win, less than the ~180s
spent on Windows shard setup and teardown.

By overriding both builders to 3 shards while leaving Linux Tests
(dbg)(1) unchanged, we cut per-shard setup overhead without hurting CQ
latency.

This frees up bot capacity on Windows and macOS pools.

Android: Use GN metadata for generate_r_java()'s R.txt files

Collect R.txt inputs for library R.java generation via GN metadata
instead of .rtxt.build_config.json (moving dist_aar()'s R.txt list into
.res.build_config.json).

This lets R.java generation start as soon as its resource inputs are
ready, without waiting for write_build_config.py or unrelated resource
targets. For chrome_java__rjava (on a default Android x64 build), this
reduces transitive Ninja build steps from 562 to 437 (and transitive
inputs from 16,004 to 14,637) and eliminates 515 .rtxt.build_config.json
outputs.

[Omnibox] Guard UrlBar.setTextWithTruncation against null LayoutParams

UrlBar.setTextWithTruncation dereferenced getLayoutParams().width
without checking for null. When setTextWithTruncation is invoked
before the view is attached to a parent ViewGroup (or after
detachment), getLayoutParams() returns null and throws a
NullPointerException.

Guard against null LayoutParams and fall back to setText(text),
matching the existing WRAP_CONTENT early-return path, and add a
Robolectric unit test covering the detached UrlBar case.

[download] Keep the temp dir out of the sanitization test

Away from a ChromeOS device the removable media mount point is
/tmp/chromeos/media/removable, and SanitizeDownloadTargetPath() accepts
anything under the temp directory when SkyVault is on. With TMPDIR
unset base::GetTempDir() answers /tmp, so that rule swallowed the
removable media root the test expects to be rejected.

The test now points TMPDIR at a directory of its own. It goes through
the environment because GetTempDir() reads TMPDIR rather than DIR_TEMP,
so a ScopedPathOverride has no effect on it.

#ai-assisted

`TabMenuModel::AppendAiModeItems()` previously reused the Glic button
icon (`IDR_GLIC_BUTTON_VECTOR_ICON`) from `AppendGlicItems()`, causing

[Omnibox] Catch SecurityException in showSpeechRecognitionIntent

Some OEM or third-party speech recognition activities are not exported
or require permissions that Chrome does not hold, causing
WindowAndroid.showCancelableIntent to throw SecurityException (which
also surfaces as a RuntimeException when delivered from a permission
request callback).

Catch SecurityException in
VoiceRecognitionIntentHandler.showSpeechRecognitionIntent and return
false so Voice Plate falls back to the system recognizer and system
recognizer failures show R.string.voice_search_error, record
Omnibox.VoiceSearch.IntentLaunchResult, and report voice availability
impacted instead of crashing.

[OmniboxEverywhere] Push DSE branding to Omnibox Everywhere

Omnibox Everywhere hardcoded the Google G icons and the "Search Google
or type a URL" placeholder in the WebUI. To prepare for default search
engine (DSE) swappability and the `DefaultSearchProviderEnabled=false`
enterprise policy, compute DSE branding in the browser, seed it in
`loadTimeData`, and push updates to the page over Mojo.

`OmniboxEverywhereHandler::GetSearchEngineInfo()` computes the active
DSE's localized placeholder and light/dark icon paths from
`GetDefaultSearchProviderIcon()`, or null when there is no DSE. Google
keeps the gradient G in light mode and the monochrome G in dark mode;
other engines get their favicon, or the loupe when they have none.
`OmniboxEverywhereUI` seeds these values in `loadTimeData` when the
WebUI data source is created so cold starts render the right icon and
placeholder immediately without a loupe flash, matching how profile
avatar info is plumbed. `OmniboxEverywhereHandler` also sends
`SetSearchEngineInfo` on construction and on `TemplateURLService`
changes to keep open pages up to date.

`omnibox-everywhere-app` initializes its `searchEngineInfo_` from
`loadTimeData`, updates it on Mojo pushes, and binds it into
`omnibox-everywhere-omnibox`, which is re-created on every Composebox
mode switch. With AI Mode off, the input shows the DSE placeholder;
with AI Mode on, the rotating AI Mode hints still apply. When `info`
is null, the page shows the loupe, an empty placeholder, and no voice
search button.

In Chrome-branded builds, while Omnibox Everywhere remains gated on
Google DSE, there is no visible change.

parent
d72c274ee1d530f90472acf72cc87822bc3c8346 [ diff ] 
webview: Keep the back/forward cache when a WebContent moves

AwSettings flushes the back/forward cache whenever a preference changes.
The logic is that it could change the page enough to make the cache
invalid. When a WebContent moves to a new view, AwContents turns
supported hardware accelerated features (just accelerated 2D canvas) off
on detach and back on on attach.

WebSurface doesn't support full screen so it calls
setForceFullscreenUnsupported() to force disable this while it is
mounted.

Both update WebKit preferences, every move or WebSurface unmount throws
away any pages that could have been restored on back.

It is safe to skip flushing for these toggles because Blink receives
updated WebPreferences on restore, the canvas behaviour itself does not
change, and fullscreen support on a WebSurface does not affect cached
history entries (we exit fullscreen before navigating away).

To avoid changing behaviour for classic WebViews, skipping the flush on
the hardware-acceleration toggle is gated behind
AwSettings.setClearBfCacheOnHardwareAcceleration() and only turned off
on the WebContentBuilder path for now. setForceFullscreenUnsupported()
skips the flush directly since it is only ever called by AwWebSurface.

Extend expiring CriticalUserJourney histograms to 2027-11-23

Ten CriticalUserJourney histogram definitions expire on 2027-01-01,
which would stop telemetry collection for active Top Chrome critical
user journeys such as Customize Chrome, Read Anything, Tab Search, and
Settings Glow Up.

Update expires_after from 2027-01-01 to 2027-11-23 (one year out) for
all ten expiring definitions in critical_user_journeys/histograms.xml
so step transition durations and step actions continue recording across
all thirteen active journeys.

[BottomSheet] Use built-in handlebar in PwaInstallBottomSheet

PwaInstallBottomSheet previously inflated its own drag_handlebar
ImageView inside pwa_install_bottom_sheet_content.xml and manually
handled clicks on it in PwaBottomSheetController#onClick(), duplicating
the drag handle presentation and toggle behavior now provided by the
bottom sheet framework.

Override BottomSheetContent#showHandlebar() to return true in
PwaInstallBottomSheetContent, remove the custom drag_handlebar view and
its click listener binding in PwaInstallBottomSheetView, and replace
View.OnClickListener on PwaBottomSheetController with a dedicated
install button click lambda (onInstallButtonClicked()). Because the
framework positions sheet content below the built-in handlebar and adds
the handlebar height to custom peek heights, collapse the now
single-child toolbar FrameLayout into its LinearLayout with 6dp top and
bottom padding so mobile spacing and peek height stay unchanged.
Click-to-toggle parity is preserved by
BottomSheetCoordinator#toggleSheetState(), which toggles PEEK and FULL
states when HALF is disabled by WRAP_CONTENT.

Update unit and integration tests to verify showHandlebar() and
interact with the built-in handlebar view.

[chromebox_for_meeting] Report bad Mojo message for restricted ProvideAdaptor

Follow-up hardening and review cleanup for restricted CfmServiceContext
receivers:

- Report a bad Mojo message via receiver_set_.ReportBadMessage() instead
  of replying false when a restricted receiver calls ProvideAdaptor(),
  rather than logging attacker-controlled interface names or leaving a
  compromised caller's pipe connected. (CfmServiceContext stays a single
  interface because the .mojom is [Stable] and shared with the
  out-of-tree hotline daemon and extension bindings.)
- Scope dbus/object_proxy.h in cpp/ash/DEPS to *_unittest.cc via
  specific_include_rules.
- Replace banned TaskEnvironment::RunUntilIdle() with explicit
  mojo::Remote::FlushForTesting() and mojo::test::BadMessageObserver.
- Add missing <cstdint> includes and fix CfmServiceContext doc casing.

[Glic] Check GlicEnabling readiness before ClankGlicContextMenu flag

Evaluate GlicEnabling.isReadyForProfile(profile) and each entry
point's prerequisites (side panel or bottom sheet, GlicShareImage)
before querying ChromeFeatureList.CLANK_GLIC_CONTEXT_MENU (and move
tab-strip gating into GlicContextMenuUtils.shouldShowGeminiOnTabStrip)

points do not activate the Finch study on menu trigger.

[🌷] Deflake RuntimeGetContextsApiTest#GetServiceWorkerContext

Resolves root cause: Test race in
RuntimeGetContextsApiTest::SetUpExtension()
(chrome/browser/extensions/api/runtime/runtime_apitest.cc:990):
LoadExtension() is called with default LoadOptions
(wait_for_registration_stored = false), so the test proceeds and
invokes browsertest_util::StopServiceWorkerForExtensionGlobalScope()
before the extension service worker registration is stored and
promoted to active_version(). FindReadyRegistrationForScope() finds
only an installing registration (include_installing_version = false)
and invokes the test helper StopServiceWorkerForRegistration()
(content/public/test/service_worker_test_helpers.cc:118-130) with
(kErrorNotFound, nullptr), which skips DCHECK_EQ on
dcheck_always_on=false release builds and dereferences a null
ServiceWorkerRegistration pointer.

infra: Add project-chromium-tryjob-access to configs.validator

As-is, non-googlers touching //infra/config/ hit "PermissionDenied"
errors from luci-config when running `git cl presubmit` locally. So
they have to bypass presubmit hooks on upload, eg:
https://crrev.com/c/7032704

So this adds project-chromium-tryjob-access to "role/configs.validator"
so external contributors with tryjob access can run presubmit locally.

This should be safe since:
- Binding it in chromium's "@root" realm scopes it strictly to
  "projects/chromium". (ie: It gives zero access to internal projects
  or service config sets.)
- Anyone in project-chromium-tryjob-access can already upload
  //infra/config/ changes with --bypass-hooks and trigger
  linux-presubmit via CQ+1. That runs the exact same ValidateConfigs
  call and prints the output publicly anyway.

Only run Indigo page heuristics for locally eligible users

The local product metadata heuristic ran on page loads even for users
who could never be offered Indigo, such as signed-out users. It is now
skipped while the profile is not locally eligible. If a profile becomes
eligible while a page is already loaded, for example because the Indigo
component finished loading after session restore or the user signed in,
the page is classified at that point, resuming from whichever loading
milestones it has already reached.

Optimization Guide registration moves to the profile service, so that
hints fetched during navigation cover Indigo even if the profile isn't
otherwise eligible yet, and the decision is available if the profile
becomes eligible later. Once region filtering is enforced, clients
outside supported regions will also skip the heuristic and will no
longer register or query Optimization Guide for Indigo. Until then,
region doesn't affect either.

This narrows the population recorded in the
Indigo.Discovery.MetadataKeywordHeuristic histogram to locally eligible
users.

[fontconfig] Define HAVE_POSIX_MEMALIGN in meson-config.h

Fontconfig uses the low bit of pattern value pointers to tag
serialized cache offsets, so a string at an odd address is decoded as
an offset. GWP-ASan can return a right-aligned, odd pointer for the
1-byte strdup("") in FcStrCopy(), which crashes the browser process in
FcStrHashIgnoreCase() during font matching.

Upstream fontconfig fixed this in 8837b2ac ("Fix crash on
odd-addreessed pattern strings") by allocating strings with
posix_memalign() when HAVE_POSIX_MEMALIGN is defined. That commit was
already rolled in, but the checked-in meson-config.h was not
regenerated, so the bundled build still used strdup(). Add the define
that meson generates for Linux.

Fix clipped text in the Incognito history disclaimer bubble

The history disclaimer variant of IncognitoClearBrowsingDataDialog had
a single-line primary label, which elided the header with larger UI
fonts (e.g. the 11pt default font on gLinux). Its secondary label was
sized with SizeToFit() to the full bubble width, but the bubble's
content area is narrower by the dialog margins, so the label got a
height for fewer lines than it needed and was clipped at the top and
bottom.

Make both labels multi-line and drop SizeToFit(), matching the default
bubble variant (fixed in crrev.com/c/6973498).

[Translate] Prevent async language detection from disabling page action

In TranslatePageActionInteractiveUiTest, the test manually sets
GetLanguageState()->SetTranslateEnabled(true) on the initial about:blank
tab before exercising the translate page action. When the renderer for
the initial about:blank tab asynchronously completes layout and sends
ContentTranslateDriver::RegisterPage,
ChromeTranslateClient::OnLanguageDetermined() invokes
BrowserCommandController::TabStateChanged(), which recomputes
kActionShowTranslate's enabled state as false (since about:blank cannot
be translated) and hides the translate page action icon mid-test.

Navigate to a minimal page with lang="fr" and wait for language
detection to complete via TranslateWaiter before forcing
SetTranslateEnabled(true) so late language detection IPCs do not
override the test's manual translate state.

[MChips] Update the composeplate chip combinations

The merchandising chips experiment shows one of three chip combinations
next to the AI Mode button on the NTP composeplate: the incognito chip,
the create image and incognito chips, or the add image and incognito
chips. The experiment now needs the add image chip to take the place of
the incognito chip, and a fourth combination with both image chips.

In this CL:
- Add the chrome://flags variation for action_chips=4, the add image and
  create image chips.
- Show the chips on the composeplate's optional and trailing buttons.
  The four combinations are:
  1) AIM chip + incognito
  2) AIM chip + create image + incognito
  3) AIM chip + add image
  4) AIM chip + add image + create image
- The trailing button is always visible, while the optional button is
  only visible in the 3 chips layout, so the layouts with two and three
  buttons don't change.
- When image generation isn't allowed, for 2), hide the create image
  chip  i.e. AIM chip + incognito is shown, rather than falling back
  to the add image chip. For 4), AIM chip + add image is shown.
- Show the composeplate when incognito mode is disabled, if the add
  image chip takes the place of the incognito chip. This depends on
  whether the DSE is Google, so it is recomputed on that change even
  when the third party AI Mode entry point is enabled.
- Apply the AI Mode button's config even while the composeplate is
  hidden. The config and the search provider info are updated
  separately, and the composeplate's visibility now depends on both, so
  a config that arrives first would otherwise be dropped.
- Check the allowed tools when the chips are updated for Google, rather
  than only when the composeplate is created, since no Composebox
  session can be created with another DSE.

The image chips are still shown only when the DSE is Google and the
device supports the fusebox. Otherwise the incognito chip is shown alone.
Screenshots: http://shortn/_MfA1lNTcp1.

[ui/base] Add check to ui_l10n FormatString

This will make the linked bug go from crashing within GetStringFUTF16 to
FormatString, I think we should not remove this check as we could have a
resources bundle bug here. I will try to investigate it further.

The problematic message id that caused the crash was
IDS_DOWNLOAD_BUBBLE_SUPPRESS_PARTIAL_VIEW_SETTINGS_REMINDER which I
checked and all the definitions in chrome/app/resources/ are non-empty
and do have a parameter. Therefore, the bug must be within
resources-bundle that is possibly returning an empty string.

DumpWithoutCrashing() is being added to resources-bundle code so more
info can be obtained.

P.S.: Simply going to the old code that had a DCHECK will take us back
to a place where the crash happens in the vector `[]` operator, see
ui/base/l10n/localized_strings.cc line 170 here.

[iOS][Intelligence] Guard float-to-int casts in APC proto wrappers

Guard JavaScript number extraction and coordinate scaling across
//ios/chrome/browser/intelligence/proto_wrappers against C++
[conv.fpint] float-to-integer undefined behavior and 32-bit MediaData
timestamp truncation:

- Replace both ReadJsNumber helpers with a templated ReadJsNumber<T>
  checked via base::IsValueInRangeForNumericType<T> and
  base::checked_cast<T>, returning std::nullopt on out-of-range JSON
  doubles while preserving sub-pixel truncation toward zero.
- Read int64 MediaData duration and current-position millisecond fields
  via ReadJsNumber<int64_t> instead of truncating to int.
- Saturate accumulated cross-site iframe offsets in FrameGrafter with
  base::saturated_cast<int32_t>.
- Validate scrollViewProxy.zoomScale with std::isfinite and saturate
  screenshot_size and zoomed iframe_info bounding boxes in
  PageContextWrapper with base::saturated_cast<int32_t>.

Also switch the DictValue ReadJsNumber key parameter to std::string_view
and deduplicate the scrollViewProxy lookup in
-applyRedactionsAndEncodeScreenshot:.

63523f618e90f960d56cc57e7e338cf40b87db00 [ diff ] 
Use stub start time for isolated browser startup metrics

In isolated mode, the initial chrome.exe acts as a stub that loads
chrome.dll and invokes elevation_service over COM to launch the real
isolated browser. Anchoring startup metrics to the isolated process's
own entry point omits the stub, COM, and elevation overhead, making
metrics like `Startup.FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3` appear
artificially fast.

Pass the stub's entry-point QPC timestamp to the isolated browser via a
new allowlisted `--isolated-stub-start-qpc-us` switch.
`StartupTimestamps::exe_entry_point_ticks` is changed to
`std::variant<base::TimeTicks, base::TimeDelta>` so Windows chrome.exe
passes the QPC delta across the DLL boundary and `ChromeMainDelegate`
resolves it into chrome.dll's `TimeTicks` clock domain, for both
high-res and low-res clients.

This CL does not intend to affect any metrics for non-isolated browsers,
and just corrects the incorrect metric for isolated browsers.

[webauthn] Add Permissions API plumbing for remoteClientDataJSON

Register the "publickey-credentials-remote-client-data-json" permission
so that navigator.permissions.query() recognizes it when the
WebAuthenticationRemoteClientDataJson runtime feature is enabled. The
matching Permissions Policy feature landed in crrev.com/c/7850876.

The permission is not user-grantable. It has no prompt, and no Site
Settings or Page Info entry. Its content setting defaults to BLOCK.
Until a follow-up CL registers a permission context that derives the
state from enterprise policy, queries resolve to "denied".

The permission is undelegated, as for notifications: a frame's state is
keyed on its own origin, not the top-level origin. This matches
WebAuthn, which authorizes remoteClientDataJSON by the caller origin, so
once the follow-up context is registered, query() in a cross-origin
iframe reports the decision WebAuthn enforces. The embedder still
controls use through Permissions Policy delegation.

Blink and content:
- Add the PermissionName, PermissionType (value 47) and descriptor
  mappings in both directions.
- Map the permission to its Permissions Policy feature, so frames
  without the feature are denied.
- Throw a TypeError for the descriptor while the runtime feature is
  disabled.

Permissions and content settings:
- Use PermissionDelegationMode::kUndelegated for the permission.
- Register PUBLIC_KEY_CREDENTIALS_REMOTE_CLIENT_DATA_JSON as unsyncable,
  scoped to the requesting origin, and limited to secure origins, with
  UMA value 149.
- Register it on desktop only for now. Android support is tracked in
  crbug.com/506062130, and the Android-only test expectations are
  guarded accordingly.

Embedders and tools:
- Deny the permission in WebView, content_shell and headless_shell.
  headless_shell otherwise reports every permission as "prompt", but it
  never prompts for or authorizes this one.
- Classify it as UI-less in Site Settings.
- Leave it out of the DevTools permission types: an override would only
  change the query() result, never WebAuthn authorization.
- Update the exhaustive permission lists in the Controlled Frame and
  headless tests.
- Delegate it in the PrivilegedWebContents content-settings policy, like
  the other web permissions.

Tests cover the cross-origin iframe case on both sides: the permission
uses the iframe's own origin (PermissionManagerTest), and WebAuthn
authorizes the iframe's origin (WebAuthRequestSecurityCheckerTest). A
tentative WPT checks the permission's name and default "denied" state.

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code and GitHub
Copilot) and reviewed and tested by the author. Please look closely at
the content-setting parameters (scope, incognito inheritance, origin
restriction), the undelegated mode, and at the desktop-only registration
and its Android test guards.

Bug: 506062130
Test: blink_unittests --gtest_filter=PermissionsTest.*
Test: content_unittests --gtest_filter=*PermissionControllerImpl*:*PermissionUtilTest*:*WebAuthRequestSecurityChecker*
Test: components_unittests --gtest_filter=PermissionManagerTest.*
Test: android_webview_unittests --gtest_filter=AwPermissionManagerTest.*
Test: headless_browsertests --gtest_filter=*KnownPermissionTypes*
Test: headless_unittests --gtest_filter=HeadlessPermissionManagerTest.*
Test: virtual/remote-client-data-json-policy/external/wpt/webauthn/remote-client-data-json-permission.tentative.https.html

fuzzilli: Treat error pages as failed navigations

ui_test_utils::NavigateToURL() returns the main frame of whatever
committed, including an error page [1]. The startup navigation then
passed its CHECK, and programs ran on the error page, where no Mojo
bindings are loaded.

Navigate with content::NavigateToURL(), which fails unless a normal page
committed at the requested URL [2]. Also check if an error page is still
loaded.

[1]: https://crsrc.org/c/chrome/test/base/ui_test_utils.cc;l=389-401;drc=227d092a0d8dde48c3f186595f557e6142752e42

Remove unused system_cpu::CpuProbe from PageResourceMonitor

PageResourceMonitor creates a system_cpu::CpuProbe at startup and
requests samples on every 2-minute collection cycle, even though
OnPageResourceUsageResult no longer reads the system_cpu parameter
since https://crrev.com/c/5732134 removed the expired intervention
evaluation histograms.

On Windows, starting a second concurrent CpuProbeWin during browser
startup contends on pdh.dll!GetMachine and ntdll!LdrpLoaderLock with
CpuHealthTracker's probe.

Remove CPUResultConverter, delayed_cpu_result_converter_, and the
//components/system_cpu dependency from PageResourceMonitor, computing
per-tab CPU proportions directly on the PerformanceManager sequence.

gl: Demote repeated DXGI output lookup failures to DVLOG(1)

On headless Windows GCE bots with no matching display output,
VSyncThreadWinDXGI retries the DXGI output lookup on every vsync tick.
With DCHECKs enabled, those two DLOG(ERROR) calls flood test logs until
long browser tests fail with EXCESSIVE_OUTPUT.

By changing both logs to DVLOG(1), we keep the diagnostics available
when needed without spamming default test output

This stops passing Windows browser tests from hitting log size limits.

[Unified Tabstrip] Use overlap to set bounds of animating views

Previously, we set the starting/target bounds of adding/closing views to
the midpoint of surrounding views. This was an approximation of the
intended behavior due to losing information about the layout at the
animating layout manager level.

In order to get the bounds to exactly match the original horizontal
tabstrip, we have to introduce a dependency on tab strip layout utils.
GetChildOverlap is changed to also apply to tab groups (and should
already apply to the pinned container without making any changes).

ContainerTiming: move ownership from the window to PaintTiming

ContainerTiming was a LocalDOMWindow supplement, while its records and
paint attribution are about one document. When a document reuses the
window of the initial empty document, it inherited that state.

Make PaintTiming own it, as it owns ElementTiming, and create it on
first use through PaintTiming::EnsureContainerTiming(). Each document
now starts with a fresh ContainerTiming.

Scope DevTools Target.createTarget to the session's BrowserContext

Update TargetHandler::CreateTarget in content and desktop chrome to
resolve the target Profile or BrowserContext from the session's
DevToolsAgentHost when invoked on non-Browser sessions. Previously,
omitting browserContextId fell back to the last-used Profile or default
BrowserContext, and explicit browserContextId values were accepted on
non-Browser sessions, allowing targets to be created in a different
context than the attached session. Non-Browser sessions now reject
browserContextId and scope target creation to the host's own
BrowserContext.

Additionally, add a null check for web_contents() in
WebContentsDevToolsAgentHost::GetBrowserContext() to safely handle
detached WebContents instances, add a headless protocol test for page
sessions, and add a browser test for chrome.debugger extension
sessions.

The Android TargetHandler is updated in a follow-up CL.

[Navigation API] Preserve initiator activation on intercept()

Previously, committing an intercepted navigation via
NavigateEvent::CommitNow() queried the target frame's live transient
user activation rather than preserving the initiator frame's activation
state captured when the navigation started. This allowed a gesture-less
cross-origin frame or deferred precommitHandler to inherit the target
frame's transient user activation.

Record has_transient_user_activation on NavigateEventDispatchParams at
navigation dispatch time and forward it to
DocumentLoader::RunURLAndHistoryUpdateSteps() so committed navigations
attribute user activation to the actual initiator.

Fix Mac control+click handling in WebUI toolbar

Several controls interpreted this similar to a left-click, but it should
be interpreted as a right-click. This was mostly a simple change with
two interesting quirks:
1. content settings were incorrectly ignoring control+click, so they're
   modified to handle it correctly.
2. location bar word selection behavior regressed when I changed
   isOnlyLeftClick() to ignore control+click on Mac, so I decided to
   leave the location bar unmodified.

[BottomSheetHandles] Use built-in handlebar in setup list sheet

EducationalTipSetupListBottomSheetContent previously embedded a custom
drag_handle_bar ImageView inside its XML layout instead of using the
bottom sheet framework's built-in handlebar. This bypassed centralized
handlebar styling, hover/click handling, and desktop layout support.

Override showHandlebar() to return true in
EducationalTipSetupListBottomSheetContent, remove the custom
drag_handle_bar ImageView from
educational_tip_setup_list_see_more_bottom_sheet_layout.xml, and flatten
the redundant outer LinearLayout into the root ScrollView with the
existing padding moved onto its child LinearLayout so overflowing items
are not clipped while scrolling. Keep the 8dp top padding dimension to
preserve the 24dp gap below the handlebar on phone layouts, and keep the
shared drag handle dimensions and drawable because other sheets still
reference them.

Update testShowBottomSheet() in
EducationalTipSetupListBottomSheetCoordinatorUnitTest to verify
showHandlebar() returns true and the content layout is flattened to a
root ScrollView.

[ozone] Don't range-check DRM modifier halves as EGLint

NativePixmapEGLBinding::InitializeFromNativePixmap() pushed the low
and high 32 bits of the format modifier through
base::checked_cast<EGLint>(), which CHECK-fails when a half has bit 31
set. AMD GFX8 (Polaris) modifiers from recent Mesa, such as
0x02000001D0CA0400, hit this and crash the GPU process.

EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import_modifiers expects the raw bit pattern of
each half, so reinterpret the uint32_t halves as EGLint with
base::bit_cast instead. Offsets keep the checked conversion.

(ViewUtils.waitForStableView) in renderTiles() and after orientation
changes before capturing RenderTest snapshots. Previously,

fuzzilli: Add generators following chains of reply remotes

Remotes returned in replies were rarely used, as using one requires an
await, a property retrieval and a method call in the same scope.

Emit one CodeGenerator per maximal chain of replies from each remote.
Each generator runs in async functions, awaits every call of the chain,
and leaves the remotes in scope for the other generators. The chains
share a weight of 5000.

begin main frames after LayerTreeHostImpl destruction by timing
ViewTransition calls with the SendEarlyFinalBeginMainFrame feature
enabled.

This CL closes the loophole.

[TTC][System Volume][3/8] Read the output volume on ChromeOS

Implements OutputVolumeMonitor on ChromeOS with CrasAudioHandler, which
already runs in the browser process. The monitor reports the system
output mute state and the output volume only when either value changes.
Without an active output node, GetState() returns nullopt.

CrasAudioHandler does not notify observers when policy or the security
curtain forces mute, so the callback misses those changes.

[iOS] Hide minimized Assistant container offscreen with bottom omnibox

When UseSceneViewController is disabled (e.g.
--disable-field-trial-config) and the omnibox is at the bottom,
AssistantContainerViewController.view is anchored above the bottom
toolbar with safeAreaInsets.bottom == 0 and clipsToBounds == NO.
Entering fullscreen only translated the minimized container by its own
height + margin, leaving it overlapping the collapsed bottom omnibox.

Clip the container view to its bounds (matching SceneViewController) and
extend the fullscreen translation by the distance from the container
superview bottom to the window bottom so the minimized container moves
completely offscreen.

Videos (legacy / --disable-field-trial-config):
- Before (bug):
  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cGxauHjagylR-yCY7_ynh_nf7m1rJtak/view
- After (fix):
  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hkbHnqMM9-yYXYMkZUYFNXpei0QYmJn6/view

Videos (ChromeNextIa + UseSceneViewController enabled):
- Before:
  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_9JKguAq1APr1SUSq4unFqKABVweIM5c/view
- After:

[iOS] Add Account Switching promo display handler

This CL:
- adds `AccountSwitchingPromoDisplayHandler` and registers it in
  `PromosManagerCoordinator`,
- adds `-showAccountSwitchingPromo` to `PromosManagerCommands`,
- implements it in `BrowserModalHost`, which calls the new
  `-showAccountSwitchingPromoWithIdentity:completion:` of
  `SceneSignInCommands` with the identity returned by
  `AccountSwitchingPromoSceneAgent.targetIdentity`, and calls
  `-promoWasDismissed` on completion,
- implements `-showAccountSwitchingPromoWithIdentity:completion:` in
  `SigninModalHost`, which uses the new
  `+[SigninCoordinator
  accountSwitchingPromoCoordinatorWithBaseViewController:browser:contextStyle:preselectedIdentity:]`
  factory method to present `SignInAndHistorySyncCoordinator` with
  `fullscreenPromo:YES` and this preselected identity as its
  `_signinCoordinator`.

As for `-showFullscreenSigninPromoWithCompletion:`, using
`SigninModalHost`'s `_signinCoordinator` ensures that the scene has a
single sign-in flow, that the promo is stopped when another sign-in flow
or the settings are opened, and that it is not started when the UI is
blocked. Sign-in being disabled and the scene UI being blocked are
checked before creating the coordinator, since `SigninCoordinator`'s
initializer requires sign-in to be enabled and acquires a
`ScopedUIBlocker` (which hits a `CHECK()` if another scene is blocking
the UI).

To manually test the promo on a personal profile signed into a
non-supervised, non-managed primary account with a second account on the
device:
- Set `chrome://flags/#enable-account-preview-switching-account` to
  `Enabled (Skip Cooldown)` (or pass `--enable-features` with
  `EnableAccountPreviewSwitchingAccount:SkipCooldown/true`) to enable
  the feature and bypass the 28-day sign-in cooldown and per-pair
  limits.
- Ensure `AccountPreviewDataService` has a preferred switching
  candidate.
- Either set iOS Settings > Chrome > Experimental Settings > Force Promo
  (`NextPromoForDisplayOverride`) to `Account Switching Promo`, or set
  `chrome://flags/#in-product-help-demo-mode-choice` to `Enabled` (or
  pass `IPH_DemoMode:chosen_feature/IPH_AccountSwitchingPromo` in
  `--enable-features`). In both cases, background Chrome before killing
  and relaunching it so a clean shutdown (`WasLastShutdownClean()`) is
  recorded.

The result can be seen in:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PrXFNA93c9kuUvbBVS4_6TPzeY6iIAu9/view?usp=sharing

One pager architecture: http://go/velcro-bling-account-switch-dd

Test: ios_chrome_unittests --gtest_filter=SigninModalHostTest.*
Test: ios_chrome_unittests --gtest_filter=*AccountSwitchingPromo*

[WebUI] Prefer test.skip() with <if expr> for platform-specific disables

Update docs/webui/testing_webui.md to recommend choosing between
test.skip() and test() with <if expr> on a shared function instead of
wrapping test(...) in // <if expr="not is_...">. Preprocessing out the
test body prevents TypeScript from type-checking the skipped test on
that platform and can trigger unused-import errors.

Link the disable-test skill's WebUI section directly to
docs/webui/testing_webui.md#disabling-tests instead of duplicating the
guidance.

[iOS][Prime] Start auto-submit flows minimized

Auto-submit flows in the Gemini assistant container previously opened at
the medium detent and immediately collapsed to the minimized thinking
state once submission began. Start auto-submit invocations with a
non-empty prompt directly in the minimized detent without a grabber, and
skip expanding to medium when re-invoking with an auto-submit prompt.

Starting minimized without a grabber requires supporting container state

updates:
- Sync consumer padding on UI state changes so initial minimized
  presentation has no padding even when detent-change callbacks do not
  re-fire.
- Gate zero-state dismissal on zero-state visibility rather than
  conversation absence so minimized auto-submit flows are not dismissed
  before thinking starts.
- Keep the container minimized across initial conversation-loading
  updates, while expanding on conversation-load or dormant errors
  (including an error following an initial non-error dormant status).
- Seed the session metrics manager with the initial detent so minimized
  duration, expansion, and dismissal metrics stay accurate.

2864f4e5b6ccedc3744c3d6925372b695b582605 [ diff ] 
[Public Transit] Make SyncTestRule's activity launch optional

SyncTestRule extends ChromeTabbedActivityTestRule and always launches
ChromeTabbedActivity, so suites using it cannot use the Public Transit
Fresh/AutoReset CTA rules (crbug.com/433553616).

Add a SyncTestRule(boolean launchActivity) constructor. With false, the
rule does not launch or own an activity; the test's CTA rule does, and
sync is set up through
ChromeBrowserInitializer#runNowOrAfterFullBrowserStarted once the full
browser has started.

No behavior change for existing callers: new SyncTestRule() still
launches the activity, and since the browser has then already started,
sync setup still runs synchronously in before(). Callers are migrated
in the follow-up CL.

Reland "Convert flags, metrics, autofill, zucchini actions to python_binary()"

This is a reland of commit f195011851b9d15fd640dedab620796f82159abe

Reason for reland:
Added //tools/metrics to components/cronet/android/dependencies.txt
(now a transitive GN dependency via
//base:memory_dump_provider_name_variants using python_action() with
//tools/metrics:generate_allowlist_from_histograms_file), which caused
//components/cronet/android:dependencies_checks to fail on
android-cronet-x86-rel.

Original change's description:
> Convert flags, metrics, autofill, zucchini actions to python_binary()
>
> Convert remaining >4-entry action_with_pydeps() actions in tools/ and
> components/:
> - //tools/flags and //chrome/browser (generate_expired_list)
> - //tools/metrics (generate_allowlist_from_histograms_file, which
>   extends sys.path via Path.resolve())
> - //components/autofill/core/browser (transpile_entity_schema, which
>   extends sys.path via os.path.realpath())
> - //components/zucchini/fuzzers (generate_fuzzer_data, which uses
>   Path.resolve())
>
> Also normalize ROOT_PATH with os.path.normpath() in
> tools/flags/flags_utils.py and tools/flags/generate_expired_list.py so
> generate_expired_list.pyz works on clean RBE sandboxes where
> //tools/flags/ does not exist on disk.
>

[PDF] Call PDFiumPage::PopulateImageAltText() from GetImageInfo()

Make PDFiumPage::PopulateImageAltText() private and call it from
GetImageInfo() instead of GetAccessibilityInfo(), since only
GetImageInfo() reads `images_` alt text. Also drop CalculateTextRuns()
from PopulateImageAltText() and check `marked_content_id_to_images_map_`
before FPDF_StructTree_GetForPage() so tagged pages without images skip
loading and traversing the struct tree.

[Public Transit] Modernize README and delete stale getting_started.md

getting_started.md was an uncompiled codelab that had accumulated stale
APIs (*PTTest naming, a non-compiling rule constructor,
Condition(isRunOnUiThread)) and recommended ReusedCtaTransitTestRule by
default.

Delete getting_started.md and its unused screenshot, add a short
"Write Your First Test" section to README.md alongside the compiled
Example*CtaTest classes, recommend AutoResetCtaTransitTestRule for
batching, and update stale transition and condition API names (waitFor,
waitForAnd, replaceFacility, Outcome, UiThreadCondition, hopOnTo).

Part 1 of 4 establishing updated in-tree Public Transit documentation
and the public-transit agent skill.

printing: Use txt extension for viewing PPDs

When the user views a PPD, the file is downloaded to their Downloads
directory and then opened in a new Chrome window.  In order to ensure
that the PPD is treated as plain text regardless of the system MIME
database, use a .txt extension instead of .ppd.

[Linux] Fall back to YV12 when LINEAR XB30 needs an external sampler

Since bb1213dee, VideoFrameOutputFormat() selects XB30 for 10-bit
video. XB30 frames are CPU-written LINEAR dma-bufs, and NVIDIA reports
(ABGR2101010, LINEAR) as external_only. Chromium samples them as
GL_TEXTURE_2D, so the video renders black.

Query eglQueryDmaBufModifiersEXT on Linux and clear caps.image_ab30 in
the raster decoder when LINEAR AB30 is external-only, so media falls
back to YV12. chromium_image_ab30 is left unchanged because it also
enables the GL_RGB10_A2 validators used by GL-texture shared images.

Tested on Ubuntu, GNOME Wayland, RTX 3070, driver 595.99.02:
10-bit AV1/VP9 and Netflix render correctly (were black), 8-bit video
is unchanged.

[Enterprise][Proxy] Require HTTPS for authenticated PvD proxies

Previously, ClassifyProxyAuthChallenge() ignored the challenger scheme
and assumed HTTPS, while ParseProxy() accepted non-HTTPS PvD proxy
endpoints configured with google_chrome.auth. If a higher-precedence
rule (such as ProxyOverrideRules) or a PvD route directed traffic to a
plain-HTTP proxy, Chrome could attach OAuth2 bearer tokens or honor
disguised error realms and static url= redirects over an unencrypted
proxy connection.

Require HTTPS whenever browser-handled proxy authentication is involved,
while preserving plain-HTTP proxy support when browser auth is not used:

- Reject non-HTTPS PvD proxy endpoints in ParseProxy() if
  google_chrome.auth is present with any type other than "none". In
  ParseProvisioningDomainConfig(), prune unrecognized or rejected proxy
  IDs from proxy-match rules and drop rules that have no valid proxy
  endpoints left (preserving explicit DIRECT rules) so rejected
  endpoints fall through to lower-priority rules/PAC/system proxies
  instead of producing an empty ProxyList that forces DIRECT.
- Return Decision::kNotApplicable ("non_https_challenger") in
  ClassifyProxyAuthChallenge() for non-HTTPS 407 challenges so
  extensions and the browser login prompt can still handle plain-HTTP
  proxy auth without exposing bearer tokens, rendering disguised error
  pages, or redirecting tabs via url=.
